o: Explain the steps and required conditions for linear search.
Apply the algorithm or method to supplied data.
c: Linear search inspects items in sequence, so the list does not need to be sorted.
Compare the target with the item at index 0, then increase the index if there is no match.
Stop on the first match and return/report its index, or report not found after the last item.
For n items, a search may check up to n items; finding an early match can require fewer.

k.q: Trace linear search through an unsorted list of CPU register names.
k.code:
array registers = ["ACC","MDR","PC","MAR"]
for i = 0 to 3
    if registers[i] == "PC" then
        print(i)
    endif
next i
p: Change target "PC" to "MAR" and predict again.
Recall what PC and MAR store, and explain why linear search does not require a sorted list.
k.a: PC is at index 2; MAR is at index 3. PC holds the next instruction's address; MAR holds the memory address being accessed. Linear search can examine unsorted values in order. This small snippet prints nothing if there is no match; a full algorithm should report not found.
